articles.title: Quantum Foundry Copenhagen announces 5,300-square-meter quantum chip fabrication facility
articles.description: Quantum Foundry Copenhagen and the Novo Nordisk Foundation have announced plans to establish a 5,300 sqm quantum chip fabrication facility in Copenhagen, opening in 2027 to strengthen Europe's quantum manufacturing capabilities.
articles.content: The facility will be tailored to the Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme and aims to develop a generally applicable quantum computer. It represents a significant step in building European sovereignty in quantum hardware, addressing a gap left by the dominance of US and Chinese quantum initiatives.

articles.description: The European AI Office is recruiting approximately 40 enforcement staff to build capacity ahead of the December 2, 2026 deadline for legacy AI systems to comply with Article 50(2) marking requirements.
articles.content: With 32 days of enforcement activity and no fines issued yet, the AI Office is expanding its team to oversee general-purpose AI model obligations and high-risk system compliance. The hiring round closes September 8, 2026, and signals a shift from preparation to active enforcement in Q4.

articles.title: 31.7% of Spanish enterprises show AI governance gaps in EU AI Act compliance, survey finds
articles.description: An Entelgy survey reveals that 31.7% of large Spanish enterprises lack adequate AI governance for EU AI Act compliance, highlighting significant consulting opportunities in the European AI compliance market.
articles.content: The survey also found that 86.7% of AI consulting partners foresee growth in 2026 as organisations scramble to meet compliance deadlines. The findings underscore the gap between the EU AI Act's August 2026 application date and actual organisational readiness across European enterprises, particularly in Spain where AESIA guidance adds additional compliance layers.

articles.title: NATO's next AI command-and-control architecture is emerging in the Arctic
articles.description: NATO's Task Force X-Arctic trials in Iceland are building the alliance's next AI-driven command-and-control architecture at Europe's northern edge, integrating autonomous systems and real-time platform re-tasking.
articles.content: The Arctic has become a critical theatre for NATO's AI development, with simulation work and uncrewed-systems trials testing real-time optimisation and re-tasking of platforms. The initiative reflects how NATO is integrating AI into its deterrence strategy, particularly in response to Russian activity in the European Arctic following Finland and Sweden's accession.

articles.title: US Commerce Secretary Lutnick says semiconductor tariffs are coming: 'Build in America or pay'
articles.description: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick announced the Trump administration is preparing semiconductor tariffs with carveouts for companies that build chip facilities in the United States, with implications for European semiconductor supply chains.
articles.content: The tariff framework targets companies that do not invest in US-based semiconductor manufacturing, following a 'build it here and you pay no chip tariff' approach. European chip companies and AI infrastructure providers with US operations, including TSMC Arizona and SK Hynix Indiana, could face higher costs if they do not meet US investment requirements.

articles.title: NIST taps UK's PQShield to map global rules for quantum-safe cryptography transition
articles.description: Following NIST's 2024 post-quantum cryptography algorithm standardisation, the UK-based PQShield has been selected to assist in mapping varied global rules for quantum-safe algorithm transitions, including the NSA's ban on hybrid approaches.
articles.content: PQShield's role involves harmonising post-quantum cryptography migration guidance across different national frameworks, addressing inconsistencies between the NSA's approach, EU policies, and other global standards. The work is critical as organisations worldwide face a deadline to transition from quantum-vulnerable encryption before quantum computers can break current cryptographic systems.

articles.title: Chips Act 2.0 analysis: Europe can compete in semiconductors, but not at every layer
articles.description: EE News Europe's third-part analysis of the EU Chips Act 2.0 concludes Europe can compete in semiconductors but not at every layer of the value chain, and should not treat market-share targets as an industrial strategy.
articles.content: The analysis examines Europe's semiconductor strategy following the Digital Omnibus amendments and the shift from volume targets to strategic indispensability. It argues that Europe's strength lies in specialised segments like automotive chips and MEMS, rather than competing head-on with TSMC and Samsung in leading-edge fabrication.

articles.title: Exail delivers space-grade laser for Europe's CARIOQA quantum gravimetry mission
articles.description: French photonics company Exail has delivered a space-qualified laser source to CNES for Europe's CARIOQA quantum pathfinder mission, advancing quantum sensing capabilities in space.
articles.content: The CARIOQA mission, funded by the Horizon Europe Programme, aims to demonstrate quantum sensing capabilities in orbit by operating a quantum accelerometer in space. Exail's laser source is a critical component for the quantum gravimetry Pathfinder Mission, which could enable ultra-precise Earth and climate monitoring from space.

articles.title: Apple's Siri AI launches September 9 with waitlist and complete EU block due to DMA
articles.description: Apple's rebuilt Gemini-powered Siri AI arrives on iOS 27 waitlisted and English-only, with the EU completely blocked over Digital Markets Act requirements for third-party assistant access.
articles.content: Apple confirmed the EU block stems from DMA rules requiring equal device access for rival voice assistants. Apple proposed a Trusted System Agent architecture as an alternative, but the European Commission rejected it. Approximately 450 million iPhone and iPad users in the EU are affected, with no timeline for availability. Siri AI also faces regulatory delays in China.

articles.description: EU antitrust regulators are seeking feedback from publishers on Google's proposal to let them opt out of AI search features without affecting their regular search rankings.

Google announced its AI opt-out in June 2026, the same day the UK antitrust watchdog ordered similar measures. The Commission's inquiry focuses on whether the opt-out is truly voluntary or carries hidden penalties.

articles.content: The Hamburg- and Berlin-based venture platform aims to close the funding gap between seed and growth stages for European DeepTech startups. articles.description: OpenAI says its upcoming Astra model can find and exploit previously unknown security flaws without human guidance, meeting the Critical threshold under its Preparedness Framework.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 with improved coding and cybersecurity

articles.title: EU Cyber Resilience Act reporting deadline arrives September 11 with ENISA's filing portal
articles.description: Starting September 11, 2026, manufacturers must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents through ENISA's Single Reporting Platform under the EU Cyber Resilience Act.
articles.content: The CRA introduces mandatory vulnerability and incident reporting for products with digital elements in the EU Digital Single Market. ENISA's Single Reporting Platform launches the same day reporting becomes mandatory. Manufacturers, importers, and distributors must notify ENISA and national CSIRTs within 24 hours of discovering actively exploited vulnerabilities. Non-compliance can carry fines up to 15 million euros or 3% of turnover.

articles.title: EuroHPC signs EUR387.8M contract for LUMI-AI supercomputer in Finland
articles.description: EuroHPC JU awarded French vendor Bull a EUR387.8 million contract to deploy LUMI-AI in Kajaani, the sixth AI Factory machine, aiming for a tenfold rise in AI capacity versus current LUMI.
articles.content: The system will sit at CSC Kajaani data centre and serve the LUMI AI Factory consortium of Finland, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Norway and Poland. It will use AMD Instinct MI430X GPUs and 6th-gen EPYC CPUs, with installation planned for the second half of 2027. EuroHPC and the consortium split the cost 50/50. Aimed first at European startups and SMEs.
